evidence_observations: Canonical main contains browser local Proof of Work in mining.js and an independent Node.js reference node in sovereign-forge/node/fae-node.mjs.
The reference node exposes GET /template?address=<faet1...>, GET /status, and POST /submit-block and validates double-SHA-256 work locally.
The existing independent-node smoke test already proves that a locally operated node can issue a template, accept locally computed Proof of Work, and credit the supplied public reward address.
No first-class standalone/headless miner product was found in canonical main.
Browser direct mining consumes only a reward address at the protocol boundary, but the current browser miningLoop is coupled to the browser wallet/watch-only object for product state.
Browser mining already contains authoritative tip observation, stale-work invalidation, pre-submission freshness validation, and automatic reacquisition behavior.

The imported Sovereign Forge browser snapshot is hash-pinned and root mining.js is required by CI to remain byte-identical to sovereign-forge/browser/mining.js; silently editing only one copy would violate canonical verification.
invariants: Mining requires only a selected node and a public reward address.
Seed phrases, private keys, wallet passphrases, vault material, and signing authority never enter the standalone miner.
Proof of Work executes on the mining device.
The selected node remains authoritative for template and tip state.
Consensus-facing semantics must be demonstrated equivalent to active v4 behavior before admission.
A protected/pinned browser snapshot is not rewritten merely to satisfy code-sharing aesthetics.
Retries and reconnects cannot erase rejection or failure evidence.
Execution consumes existing authority and creates none.

acceptance.node_selection: explicit endpoint with local HTTP permitted and remote HTTPS preferred
acceptance.proof_of_work: active public-testnet v4 double-SHA-256 semantics only
acceptance.parity: browser/reference-node/standalone deterministic vectors agree on canonical serialization, nonce binding, hash, leading-zero target interpretation, submission envelope, reward-address binding, and stale-tip behavior
acceptance.operations: observable real states, bounded reconnect, stale replacement, graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM, restart-safe secret-free configuration
acceptance.local_node: standalone miner mines a real block against an isolated independent reference node and reward appears at supplied address
acceptance.security: no wallet seed/private key/passphrase/signing material dependency or persistence
